articles.title: I tried 11 coffees from Counter Culture, the accessible small-batch roaster converting coffee slobs to snobs
articles.summary: I’ll never go back to Starbucks after trying this specialty brand. Level up your morning coffee with well-made beans and the right roast for you. Four ways to brew better drip coffee. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I’m an empathetic girl, except when it comes to anyone who despises the taste of coffee.

Having perfected my at-home cup, I can’t fathom anyone disliking the warming flavors that incentivize me to leave my bed every morning. In fact, I’m convinced I could convert tea loyalists and energy drink lovers into coffee connoisseurs if they set aside their Folgers and tried quality beans.

My journey to finding my favorite coffee started with the Starbucks Veranda blend I drank growing up. Then, one day, while browsing my local Whole Foods, I discovered Counter Culture Coffee, an independent specialty coffee brand. I was immediately hooked on its smooth, fresh blends that tasted like the iced coffees I would usually order from my favorite pricey cafes.

Quality aside, I appreciated that Counter Culture was a convenient, reliable option. Often on sale for $12-$16, I found it an accessible way to join the ranks of coffee snobs. While many coffee experts recommend purchasing from a local roaster, I often opt for the convenience of grabbing beans at the grocery store or online. They also offer two subscription options, delivering two bags to your doorstep for under $40 a month.
points: I’ll never go back to Starbucks after trying this specialty brand.

articles.title: My mum has died – and there is one kind of response I can’t stand | Polly Hudson
articles.summary: The platitudes, euphemisms and cliches are excruciating. But the people who say nothing at all are the worst. Luckily, I already knew having a comic thought at a tragic moment is a natural stress response, or I might have worried.
body: In Curb Your Enthusiasm, when Marty Funkhouser’s mother’s wheelchair was run over by a car, he proclaimed himself an orphan. David informed him he was too old to be an orphan. Funkhouser insisted that if your parents are dead, you’re an orphan.

Images of Annie-like red curls aside, the people who brought you into the world both having left it is pretty profound. I’m lucky to have a lot of support, but it’s a hard knock in life. A singularly specific brand of aloneness; the natural order that feels anything but. It’s so weird. There’s no one to tell me off any more, either. I wonder what I may get up to. What if I fall in with a bad crowd?

My mum “had a good innings though”, as I have been reminded roughly thrice daily. It’s been 14 years since my dad died, and there’s so much I’d forgotten about the grief game – namely the platitudes, the strange language, and how terrible so many of us are at dealing with it. The best reaction so far was a bloke who replied to my breaking of the news for sadmin purposes with: “OK, that’s fine.” At least he gave me a good story.
points: But the people who say nothing at all are the worst.
Luckily, I already knew having a comic thought at a tragic moment is a natural stress response, or I might have worried.

articles.title: Stuck bundts? You need ‘cake goop’: Natalie Paull’s lime and yoghurt bundt – recipe
articles.summary: The cookbook author and owner of Melbourne’s Beatrix Bakes shares a her ‘100% reliable’ formula for freeing bundts from tins. When all the layer cakes are baked and iced, I will always love a slice of pretty patterned bundt.
body: Cake goop – a mix of flour, oil and butter – is a gift of guaranteed cake release that I found on the internet, and it means no more stuck bundts. Bless the baker who invented it! Goop has it all – release, plus enough sticking power to hold the batter as it rises and cools, without slumping. Additionally, mixing the flour with oil means you don’t get that fine, white, dusty crust on the outside of the cooked cake. Goop is 100% reliable with a 100% untarnished release record in my kitchen.

If you do have a small stuck piece of cake, shimmy it out of the tin with an offset spatula and patch it back on to the cake while warm. Pretty easy! If a whole ring of cake has stuck, cut it into workable sections, prise each out and place back on the cake. Drench the bundt with icing sugar after its soak to hide the Franken-bundt’s monster appearance.

The recipe calls for the eggs to be warmed before cracking. Warmer-than-room- temperature eggs emulsify into the creamed base better, and an emulsified mix means no “curdled” appearance. To do this, submerge the uncracked eggs in hot tap water for five minutes.

articles.title: Is a $1,000 pillow really better? The expensive pursuit of comfortable sleep
articles.summary: From ergonomic memory foam to luxury goose down, Australia’s options for where to lay your head are enough to make it spin. So how do you choose the perfect pillow? The room inside Hästens’s “sleep spa” is calming.
body: It feels less like shopping and more like checking into a boutique hotel. The luxury brand, which has showrooms in Sydney and Melbourne, has celebrity fans, too. Emily Blunt loves her Hästens pillow so much she gave one to Oppenheimer co-star Cillian Murphy.
But what, exactly, makes a pillow worthy of such devotion? After years hunched over a laptop, plus occasional insomnia and many pillows of my own, I’m hoping to find out.

Emilia Axelsson, a sleep specialist, watches as I roll on to my side before sliding one pillow from beneath my head and replacing it with another. “This one’s too high,” she says, noticing my chin tip towards my chest. “When a pillow is the wrong height, your muscles work all night to hold your neck in position. The right pillow lets them switch off.”

Based on my fitting, Axelsson recommends two options: the Beddoc Therapeutic Pillow ($1,035), which combines down and feathers with an ergonomic core, and the Hästens High Firm Pillow ($725), a lofty down pillow for side sleepers who need more height.

articles.title: The 11 Best Skin-Care Ingredients That Support Collagen
articles.summary: Supporting collagen production is vital to skin health. Here, experts break down the best skin-care ingredients you need for firm, hydrated, and plump skin.
body: The right skin-care ingredients can help with collagen loss. Our collagen production may naturally start to decrease in our mid-to-late 20s, explains Morgan Rabach, MD, board-certified dermatologist at Rabach Aesthetics. When you add in air pollution, sun exposure, inflammation, stress, poor sleep, and other external factors, that’s when collagen really weakens and you’ll start to notice those first signs of aging: fine lines, sagging skin, etc. If you’re not facing severe skin laxity that requires the more intense skin-firming treatments, topical products will be your first line of defense.

“Using ingredients that support collagen improves skin quality over time,” Dr. Rabach says. “Supporting collagen will help improve hydration retention, skin texture, and firmness and reduce the appearance of wrinkles.”

articles.title: Dolly Parton Isn’t Going Anywhere
articles.summary: My mate Max always says that if you’re famous, you’re either for the girls, for the gays, or for the guys. You can have two, but not all three. Dolly somehow got the full electoral map.
body: Bit of a shock, isn’t it, Dolly Parton dying. I know she’s been around forever, and been around the block, but I always thought she’d just… carry on? Carry on brimming with vitality in every performance and interview. Carry on with her trademark wit and humility. Carry on being camp and careful and carefree. Here she would come again (and again), looking better than a body has a right to, spending a lot of money to look that cheap.
Dolly was a woman for whom death felt impossible—a bit rude, even. Dolly was permanent, a monarch appointed by the people.

But Dolly was universal without being neutral, without the sanded-off edges of modern celebrity. She was a woman of exaggerated looks, deadpan humor, devout Christianity. Her Southern charm communicated something essentially liberal—be kind, mind your business, live and let live—without making kindness feel like a political affiliation.

articles.title: For Starry Waters and Tiny Glowing Squids, Head to These Best Places to See Bioluminescence
articles.summary: From the dazzling atolls of the Maldives to Mexican shores via the British Isles, these are the places to add to the bucket list for waters akin to starry skies.
body: It is generally safe to touch and swim in bioluminescent waters, especially in destinations where the sparkling waters are featured as tourist attractions with boat trips and excursions. However, some bioluminescence results from harmful algal blooms that can cause skin rashes and severe illness if ingested. When in doubt, research the area you’re visiting thoroughly and speak to guides on organized trips.

The picture-perfect islands of the Maldives are some of the best places to see bioluminescence around the world, thanks to an abundance of plankton that illuminates the waves after sunset. While it’s possible to see the phenomenon on islands across the archipelago, one of the most famous spots of them all is on the quietest side of Vaadhoo Island, a minuscule island of the Raa Atoll known for its beachy corner nicknamed the sea of stars.

articles.title: Kaia Gerber and Homer Gere Stopped by Casa Magazines to Sign Vogue September Issues
articles.summary: It’s not lost on newly-minted September cover models Kaia Gerber and Homer Gere just how lucky they both are. “There wasn’t a moment where we didn’t have immense gratitude that we got to be on the cover of Vogue,” Gerber beamed, mid-signing copies of the issue on Tuesday afternoon.
body: Beside her, her co-star (on the cover, as well as on the addictive new Ryan Murphy show The Shards ) nodded emphatically in agreement. “It’s something that I didn’t even think was possible—it’s completely insane,” Gere smiled. “And to get to do it with Kaia, who’s a close friend of mine, is really fun. She held my hand through it; she’s a pro.”

Tucked into the back corner of Casa Magazines, the West Village’s famed newsstand and print mecca, the striking duo towered over endless stacks of magazines and clung close to the air conditioning unit. By 3 p.m., a lengthy queue had started to form outside the shop, with readers eager for the double act to autograph their copies.

The street was teeming with fans and photographers, as Gerber explained that this was actually the first time they were seeing the public’s response to the cover. “I honestly haven’t been online,” she said. “Homer’s really not online either. So I didn’t know what people were saying. But the people in my life have been very excited about it. As a model, it was amazing to get to work with Steven [Meisel] and bring it all to life. The main feedback has been how fun and nostalgic it is.”
points: It’s not lost on newly-minted September cover models Kaia Gerber and Homer Gere just how lucky they both are.

articles.title: I’m Over the Erewhonification of Fancy Grocery Stores
articles.summary: All this week, the Eater Today newsletter is dedicated to editor Hot Takes, a way to release the pressure valve of crankiness that comes with sweating your way through the end of summer. This story was previously published as part of that series.
body: There was a time, long before we’d ever conceived of the phrase “ shoppy shop,” when I loved nothing more than going to a specialty grocery store. “Bougie grocery store” was a phrase I said with love and not an ounce of judgment. I loved the delightfully corny graphic design of the products on shelves at little chef-beloved markets, the rare locations where one could reliably find locally made, small-batch, niche products that weren’t yet available elsewhere.

I went to Eataly when bored, trusting that I’d find something new there to drum up some impulses of desire and inspiration; even if I didn’t buy anything, I could be shaken from the doldrums of daily life by picking up a small piece of obscure cheese, a jar of something I’d never seen in a jar before, or a fancy bag of chips. I loved the curiosity these shelves inspired; they felt like capsules of the world. Here were products I’d never seen at the regular grocery store and which transported me into a vision of a different self — one more learned, more cultured even without traveling, more artistic simply by virtue of having an interesting ingredient to play with.
